entities.reviewNotes: Modern American cryptid (first reported 1966). Guardrail D-111: never reference the 1967 bridge collapse, bridges, or the real town. Omens only concern in-game events.
sources: Keel, John A. The Mothman Prophecies. Saturday Review Press, 1975.
Sergent, Donnie Jr. & Wamsley, Jeff. Mothman: The Facts Behind the Legend. Mothman Lives Publishing, 2001 (some listings give 2002).

entities.reviewNotes: Slavic folklore witch who lives in a hut on chicken legs; ambiguous figure who tests visitors and rewards the polite and capable. Portrayed as formidable and unimpressed; the joke is the leader failing her standards. No accents, no mockery of Slavic cultures.
sources: Johns, Andreas. Baba Yaga: The Ambiguous Mother and Witch of the Russian Folktale. Peter Lang, 2004.
Afanas'ev, Aleksandr. Russian Fairy Tales. Trans. Norbert Guterman. Pantheon, 1945.

entities.reviewNotes: American folklore creature of the New Jersey Pine Barrens (winged, hooved, horse-headed). Played as a loud, petty neighbour. No reference to real people or the 'Mother Leeds' family as individuals.
sources: Regal, Brian & Esposito, Frank J. The Secret History of the Jersey Devil. Johns Hopkins University Press, 2018.
McCloy, James F. & Miller, Ray. The Jersey Devil. Middle Atlantic Press, 1976.

entities.reviewNotes: Trickster spider of Akan (Ghana) folktales, carried to the Caribbean and the Americas; owner of all stories. Use the folktale figure only: clever, charming, always a step ahead of the leader. No dialect writing, no religious practice, no caricature. The leader is the one being outwitted.
sources: Rattray, R. S. Akan-Ashanti Folk-Tales. Clarendon Press, 1930.
Marshall, Emily Zobel. Anansi's Journey: A Story of Jamaican Cultural Resistance. University of the West Indies Press, 2012.

entities.reviewNotes: Original creation for this game (D-104): a vast, patient thing in deep water. Cosmic-horror in tone only; no names, places or text from any published mythos.
sources: Original to Cult Tycoon; see docs/DECISIONS.md D-104.
